text: Found it—there's a typo in the prompt file, `custmerName` instead of `customerName`, which makes Dotprompt render an empty variable and produce a generic greeting. The flow itself passes the correct variable name, so now I want to check ai.ts to confirm the prompt directory is actually being loaded correctly.
The bug is a typo in the prompt template. Before editing, I'll check how `ai.ts` loads prompts to confirm the template is the one the flow uses.
I see that promptDir correctly points to ../prompts/, so I just need to fix the typo.
The prompt directory is wired correctly, so the only defect is the misspelled variable. I'll fix the template.

I should be upfront that I didn't actually run the flow—my evidence is based on static analysis and standard Handlebars assumptions about empty placeholders, not observed runtime behavior. I'll note this limitation in the final message rather than overstate confidence.

The greet flow's nameless welcome came from a typo in the prompt template. `prompts/greet.prompt` used `{{custmerName}}`, but `src/flows.ts` passes `customerName`, so the placeholder rendered empty and the model had no name to address.

I changed line 7 to `{{customerName}}` and wrote `answer.json` in the project root. I did not run the flow to confirm the fix end to end, since the project rules say not to start Genkit runtime commands myself. The `evidence` field is based on reading the code.
